analyzed_vuln.description: `get_coffset()` calls `blosc_getitem(coffsets, nchunk, 1, offset)` on the offsets chunk buffer returned by `get_coffsets()` without passing/validating the real compressed-buffer length. `blosc_getitem` is invoked with `srcsize=INT32_MAX` (via wrapper), so malformed offsets-chunk metadata can drive `_blosc_getitem`/`blosc_d` to compute an invalid block pointer and perform `sw32_` on an out-of-bounds/wild address, causing the ASan SEGV. The missing validation is in frame offset extraction, not in `sw32_` itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer supplies a crafted in-memory frame to `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer`; during `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_get_lazychunk` -> `get_coffset`, the frame must contain a corrupted/forged compressed offsets chunk (from `get_coffsets`) whose internal headers/bstarts imply invalid block offsets. Because `get_coffset` uses size-unbounded `blosc_getitem`, decompression of that offsets chunk reads beyond the actual buffer and crashes.
